articles.headline: Newcomers Jaylen Waddle, Jonah Coleman lead Broncos to win
articles.description: The Broncos mostly stood pat this offseason, keeping most of the 2025 roster together. But it was two newcomers on offense who helped them beat the Jaguars.
articles.body:
DENVER -- The Denver Broncos had a couple things atop their to-do list entering this past offseason. They wanted more impact at wide receiver and more production behind running back J.K. Dobbins. And the players they brought into fill both those needs -- veteran wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and rookie running back Jonah Coleman -- were integral in helping the Broncos (1-1) to their first win of the 2026 season.

"I'm proud of those guys," Broncos All-Pro left tackle Garett Bolles said. "That's why they're here, to do what they do."

In Denver's 20-13 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Waddle finished with eight catches for 138 receiving yards, including a 49-yard catch in the second quarter and a key 29-yard reception on the Broncos' final, seal-the-win possession. And they asked Coleman to carry the running game when it was time to close out the Jaguars (1-1).

Waddle had the most receiving yards by a Bronco in a single game since Jerry Jeudy had 154 in the 2022 season finale. It was also the most receiving yards by a Broncos player in his home debut since Rick Upchurch had 153 in 1975.

"Significant, right?" Broncos coach Sean Payton said of Waddle's impact, for which the sixth-year receiver earned the game ball. "You can see the explosiveness, run after the catch. Glad he's ours."

Waddle's explosion came after a quiet Week 1 debut in which he had only one reception for 2 yards in a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on "Monday Night Football." Sunday was exactly what the Broncos envisioned when they sent three draft picks, including a first-rounder, to the Miami Dolphins this past March to acquire the 27-year-old.

Payton said Sunday that Waddle's impact goes beyond stats because his explosiveness forces defenses to make decisions about when and where to bring more defenders to help on the receiver. The Broncos' only touchdown in their season-opening loss in Kansas City came when multiple defensive backs bracketed Waddle, leaving tight end Evan Engram open for a receiving score. The Broncos were able to isolate Waddle in several 1-on-1 match-ups Sunday, including the 49-yarder.

"They're a zone coverage team by nature, [but] we caught them in some man looks," Payton said. "... [Waddle] had one of those breakout games, it was great to see. He's kind of infectious, he doesn't have bad days, he likes football, he's a real good teammate. We needed it."

The Broncos also needed a spark in the running game on Sunday after Dobbins left in the third quarter with a left hamstring injury. Second-year running back RJ Harvey was already unavailable, also due to a hamstring injury. The Broncos struggled in the run game last season after Dobbins suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 10, which caused Payton to search for a reserve running back with similar traits to Dobbins.

articles.headline: Titans trying to 'trust the process' after tough loss to Eagles
articles.description: The Titans could have a 1-1 record but they're 0-2 because they didn't finish on both sides of the ball down the stretch.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. --  Tennessee Titans defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons sat at his locker still in full uniform in disbelief almost 40 minutes after watching the Philadelphia Eagles celebrate Darius Cooper's game-winning, 3-yard touchdown reception with nine seconds left on the clock. These types of tough losses can send a team spiraling, especially a team like the Titans, who's 25.9-year-old average age is tied with the Green Bay Packers, Jacksonville Jaguars and New England Patriots for the fifth-youngest roster in the league. Titans coach Robert Saleh isn't a believer in moral victories, but he refuses to allow the 24-20 loss to the Eagles alter his approach.

"You can't let the result affect your process," Saleh said. "There is no good job in losing. You're either winning or you're losing. But you can't let that deter you from the process at which you attack it because that's the only chance you have to win a football game, having a great process."

The Titans could have a 1-1 record, but they're 0-2 because they didn't finish on either side of the ball down the stretch. 

Tennessee had a 73.7% win probability when Tyjae Spears' 27-yard run gave the Titans the first down while facing third-and-22. The Titans got the ball to Philadelphia's 9-yard line but had to settle for Joey Slye's 33-yard field goal to take a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left in the game. Tennessee's defense was unable to protect the lead, allowing Jalen Hurts to march the Eagles 65 yards to the end zone thanks to Cooper's catch.

"It's frustrating, for sure," Titans quarterback Cam Ward said. "We want to end every drive with a touchdown. That's our goal each and every time that we step on the field is to get a touchdown. And for us not to be able to help the defense in that situation, we take that upon ourselves"

The Titans hadn't won a game since last December. They were humiliated by Saleh's former team, the New York Jets in the season opener. Now the Titans have to figure out a way to flush the bad feelings after having a win snatched from their grasp.

Second-year receiver Elic Ayomanor is taking a trust the process approach to get ready for the next game, which will be on the road against the New York Giants on Sunday. Ayomanor's faith is in the hard work he put in during the offseason and what he's going to do leading up to the game. That hard work has made Ayomanor a player Saleh referenced when asked how the Titans can weather the storm of a two-game losing streak to start the season.

Saleh said that everyone would be sick once they sat down and watched the film from the loss. The film showed exactly what Saleh thought he'd see, a failure to execute in multiple phases late in the game. But there were also plenty of shortcomings throughout the day. The Eagles were able to convert a ridiculous 11 of their 18 third-down opportunities. articles.headline: Questions emerge about the Jaguars' lack of pass rush
articles.description: After a promising opener, the Jaguars' pass-rush issues from last season re-emerged in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.
articles.body:
DENVER -- The Jacksonville Jaguars didn't sack Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix on Sunday. They hit him only three times, including just once in the fourth quarter (by edge rusher Travon Walker).

The lack of pressure -- especially late in the game -- was a major reason the Jaguars (1-1) blew a 10-point third-quarter lead and lost 20-13 at Empower Field at Mile High Stadium. Was it an aberration or a sign that 2026 will be a repeat of what happened in 2025?

And more importantly, can it be fixed -- and how?

"Hey, that's a damn good offensive line," Jaguars coach Liam Coen said of Denver's front. "I don't want to take too much away from them, but if we're going to beat a team like that, then we're going to have to create some pressure. Something that we all kind of saw Kansas City do in the game on Monday night [in Week 1 against the Broncos], and we weren't able to do that."

The Jaguars sacked Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson five times and recorded eight QB hits in Week 1. Walker and Josh Hines-Allen each had 1.5 sacks, and it was fair to begin to question whether the concern about the pass rush looking like it did in 2025 -- when the Jaguars ranked third in pressures but 27th in sacks -- was overblown. But those worries are back after Sunday's performance.

Per ESPN Research, Nix was 16-of-18 for 205 passing yards and a touchdown when the Jaguars sent four or fewer rushers. That means he was 6-of-13 for 83 yards and an interception when the Jaguars rushed five or more.

But it's a gamble to rely too much on blitzing to get pressure because it opens the defense up to big plays, especially if the rush doesn't even get to the quarterback. That happened several times against the Broncos, Coen said, but it's something the Jaguars might consider going forward.

"I think they caught us in a couple blitzes that they identified pre-snap when we were going to blitz and bring more," Coen said. "They ended up flipping the protections to pick some of that stuff up. So that's something we got to look at as well in terms of when we're bringing pressure."

Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun said the blame for the lack of pressure belongs to the entire defense, not only the pass rushers. Being better on first and second downs would have helped.

"We've got to own our details [on] first, second down," he said. "Now you're in third-and-passing situations. Sometimes they threw the ball out quick, but if you get them third and what, 12, third-and-[long], now you're really putting your ears back. We did not do that [Sunday] because we didn't own our details all the way through the downs."

Sunday's scenario was like the AFC wild-card playoff loss to the Bills in January. The Jaguars sacked Josh Allen once and hit him three times -- none of which came in the fourth quarter. Allen drove the Bills to two touchdowns to erase Jaguars' fourth-quarter leads.

articles.headline: Why there's hope Pittsburgh Steelers O-line can improve
articles.description: Pittsburgh's young group has struggled to find consistency, but with adjustments, there's still time to improve.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Moments before calling for the snap at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers surveyed the defense, paused and walked a couple of yards toward his line, quickly adjusting his protections as the play clock wound down.

Left guard Mason McCormick craned his neck back to Rodgers, engaging with the quarterback before gesturing at center Zach Frazier to his left. McCormick then pointed to running back Rico Dowdle, directing his attention to inside linebacker Robert Spillane on the other side of the line. As he walked back to the shotgun, Rodgers crossed his arms and made a shivering motion, one of his many cues to adjust the play.

Then, confusion led to a collision.

Dowdle ran to his right, preparing to throw a block in the gap between right guard Spencer Anderson and right tackle Dylan Cook.

But the pressure was coming from Rodgers' left. Completely unblocked, linebacker Christian Elliss came off the edge and smoked Rodgers, sandwiching him in the backfield with Spillane. The pair knocked the ball loose, and it bounced backwards for 36 yards as both teams struggled to secure it. Finally, left tackle Troy Fautanu jumped on the ball at the Steelers' 42-yard line to bring up fourth-and-43.

That was a microcosm of the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots.

"It's frustrating, just all around as an offense," Fautanu said after the game. "We couldn't really get anything going, and when we did, we just couldn't convert, we just couldn't score."

Rodgers, who took a total of four sacks Sunday, was also strip-sacked one more time in the loss. That time defensive tackle Christian Barmore muscled through Anderson to knock the ball loose and Elijah Ponder scooped it up for the defensive touchdown.

"They were giving us different looks, different pressures, different stunts," Fautanu said. "Obviously, the coaches go over it during the week. We've got to be able to go out there and execute and block our men regardless of if we're one-on-one. We've just got to do a better job."

Things won't get any easier for the group on Sunday as the team hosts the Cincinnati Bengals (1 p.m. ET, CBS), who are tied atop the league's leaderboard with eight sacks through two weeks.

Steelers coach Mike McCarthy on Sunday shouldered the blame, pointing to a need to refine details, improve communication and reduce volume in the game plan until the young team can get the basics down.

"Our protections weren't clean," McCarthy said. "We had opportunities, whether it was communication and breakdowns, clearly in the first half that took away some opportunities for big plays. ... The consistency of winning in the trenches, we need to be better there. But the reality of it is the detail is not there, and that's on coaching. It starts with me."

articles.headline: Tyler Shough's late-game heroics have Saints confidence soaring
articles.description: The second-year quarterback has been at his best this season when the game is on the line. Can he keep it up?
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough wouldn't quit.

Shough and the Saints lined up for a potentially game-sealing touchdown against the Ravens (1-1) on fourth-and-goal in Baltimore. As Shough dove for the plane of the goal line, a defensive player swiped at his face mask and yanked his head back.

Shough gripped the football hard as he was swallowed up in a mass of bodies, but he didn't let go.

The officials signaled touchdown, giving the Saints (1-1) the go-ahead score and eventually a 24-17 win, their first of the season.

"Yeah, that one hurt a little bit," Shough said later with a smile. "Yeah, I got kind of folded a couple times, but I was able to get in there. So we'd like to not make it as close. ... I was going to reach for it, but getting your head pulled off, it's tough."

For Saints coach Kellen Moore, it was a moment that showed Shough is "as though as they come."

"He's a really special player, but his willingness to hang in there and play the really hard downs, I think the rest of the team sees that, recognizes that. There's a lot of respect for what he's doing right now," Moore said.

It took the Saints five tries to get into the end zone after backing up from the Baltimore 2-yard line due to a penalty. But pushing through and getting the job done was a reversal of last week.

In Week 1, the Saints came up just short of beating the Detroit Lions in overtime, 31-30. That result might have been acceptable for last season's Saints, who were already in a 1-7 hole by the time Shough made his first start in Week 9. Getting any momentum from their rookie second-round pick felt like a win.

But the Saints knew they had something special in Shough going into this season, and edge rusher Chase Young said the time for accepting moral victories was over.

But after Sunday's win, the Saints blasted music in the locker room so loudly it could be heard in the adjoining conference room. Going toe-to-toe with the Ravens proved the Saints' confidence in Shough was deserved. So now New Orleans will aim to build on that momentum heading into their first home game of the season against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS).

"We can hang with anybody. Sometimes you have to learn how to win, learn how to finish. And I think we right on time," Young said. "... No more moral victories, man. We want W's, and if it come down to the wire, then we just got to tough it out. We want to win."

It was the Saints' biggest win since Shough was named the starter. He won five games leading the team in 2025, all against teams that finished the season with a losing record.

Since 2022, the Saints have beaten only four teams that finished the season with a winning record (the 2022 Seattle Seahawks and Philadelphia Eagles and the 2023 Indianapolis Colts and Tampa Bay Buccaneers).

articles.headline: How Cowboys prepared for Brazil trip to face Ravens
articles.description: Dallas picked up a key win Sunday against the Commanders before the focus quickly turned to Baltimore and Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Normally, Jerry Jones carries the confidence of a man sure of many things, but as the Cowboys owner and general manager arrived at  AT&T Stadium Sunday for the home opener against the Washington Commanders, he wasn't.

As he got out of his SUV, Jones walked over to a group of fans taking a tour of the stadium when he spotted a Commanders supporter.

"Tell 'em to be sweet to us," Jones laughed.

About five hours later, with the Cowboys beating Washington 37-20, Jones was able to smile.

"I really was worried about what it was going to be like if we did end up 0-2," Jones said. "And I can't say that I was a color of strength in my mentality coming into the game because I've got a lot of respect for the coaching over on the Washington Commander side. But having said all of that, this was a very important win for us, important to these guys who put the work in, the coaching staff for [coach Brian Schottenheimer], and I'm really proud of him."

A 10-hour flight to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on Thursday would have felt even longer had the Cowboys lost to Washington and dropped to 0-2 with two NFC East losses. Quarterback Dak Prescott knew of the importance of the victory as they now get ready to play the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS).

"We need to get this win. We need to get in the win column. We're back home. We need to win all of our games at home," Prescott said. "And you can't go 0-2 in the conference or the division, so, yeah, this was a must win."

The Cowboys' preparation for their trip to Brazil started last March when they caught wind that they would be selected to play their first international "home" game. The organization sent a team from the operations department to Brazil to look at the practice facilities and hotels available to them. They sent materials via cargo ship starting in June. Another plane filled with gear will arrive before the team this week.

After flying through the night Thursday, the Cowboys will have a quick workout on Friday at the training center for Flamengo, one of Brazil's first-division soccer clubs. On Saturday, they will get a brief look at Maracanã Stadium, where Sunday's game will be held, before holding a walkthrough in their hotel.

The players were off Monday and Schottenheimer is following a short-week plan with practices on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday before they board their American Airlines 777-300ER flight. Most of the players will have a first-class-type seat for the journey.

Since training camp, Schottenheimer has been mindful of how the Cowboys worked, since the game in Rio is followed by a Week 4 trip -- albeit short -- to the Houston Texans and then a four-day turnaround to play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a Thursday night game on Oct. 8.

articles.headline: Barcelona to return to Olympic Stadium next season as Camp Nou costs rise to €2 billion
articles.description: Barcelona will return to the Olympic Stadium for several months next season after approving another €510 million ($585m) of financing to finish the Spotify Camp Nou redevelopment project.
articles.headlineJa: カンプ・ノウの費用が20億ユーロに急増、バルセロナは来季もオリンピック・スタジアムを使用へ
articles.descriptionJa: バルセロナはスポティファイ・カンプ・ノウの改修プロジェクトを完了させるため、さらに5億1000万ユーロ（約5億8500万ドル）の資金調達を承認したことを受け、来季も数ヶ月間にわたりオリンピック・スタジアムを使用することになった。
articles.body:
Barcelona will return to the Olympic Stadium for several months next season after approving another €510 million ($585m) of financing to finish the Spotify Camp Nou redevelopment project.

Barça moved back to Camp Nou last November after two years at the Olympic Stadium, but they must move out again ahead of the start of the 2027-28 season to allow the roof to be put on the redeveloped Camp Nou.

Speaking at the club's AGM, treasurer Ferran Olivé confirmed the plan is for Barça to finish the current campaign at Camp Nou before beginning next season at the Olympic Stadium.

The Spanish champions then plan to return to Camp Nou in January 2028, for the second half of the 2027-28 season.

The capacity at Camp Nou is currently capped at 62,000, with only two of the three tiers open, although Olivé says it will increase to 75,000 before the end of the current campaign as the third tier gradually opens.

By the time Barça return to Camp Nou in 2028, the capacity will have risen to 95,000, finally hitting 105,000 ahead of the 2028-29 season, when the stadium should be completely finished.

UEFA announced last week that Barça's iconic home will host the Champions League final for the first time in 30 years in 2029, so there is little margin for further setbacks.

The stadium revamp, which began in 2023, is running with severe delays. The date for the work to be completely finished has been continually pushed back, which has hit the club financially.

As a result, Barça members had to approve a €510m ($585m) financing package over the weekend to "cover the economic impact caused by delays in the execution of the project," pushing the total cost up to almost €2 billion ($2.3b).

- Barcelona's Andreas Christensen injures thigh, doubt for next Clásico

- Women's Champions League Power Rankings: Are Barcelona favorites again?

"The operation is structured in two components," Barça announced in a statement.

"The first consists of €300m ($344m) which will enable the completion of Camp Nou, a project whose scope has expanded significantly beyond the original plans through the addition of new facilities, services, and technological solutions.

"The second component consists of €210m ($241m) to be raised through two Media Notes issuances of €105m ($120m) each. The first was issued in July 2026, while the second is scheduled for October or November 2026.

"Both issuances have maturities of up to 10 years, carry fixed interest rates, and are secured against future audiovisual revenues generated from La Liga and UEFA competitions."

Barça are reliant on finishing the project to help drive the club's revenue in the coming years.

They predict income will rise significantly thanks to "additional stadium-related revenue, including ticketing, VIP hospitality, the museum and other associated activities with the team's return to Camp Nou."

LINE: Athletics -111, Angels -110; over/under is 9 1/2 runs

BOTTOM LINE: The Los Angeles Angels visit the Athletics looking to end a three-game road skid.

Los Angeles is 60-96 overall and 26-49 in road games. The Angels have a 23-11 record in games when they hit at least two home runs.

articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールは当時のクラブ記録となる移籍金を投じてフロリアン・ヴィルツを獲得したが、数字の低さから見切りをつける人も多い。諦めるにはまだ早すぎるのか、それともリヴァプールは前へ進むべきなのだろうか？

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool, Arsenal, Man City in race for Feyenoord defender
articles.description: Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right back Givairo Read, but face competition from Arsenal and Manchester City. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：リヴァプール、アーセナル、マンCがフェイエノールトDFの争奪戦へ
articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールはフェイエノールトの右サイドバック、ヒバイロ・リードを注視しているが、アーセナルやマンチェスター・シティとの争奪戦に直面している。『Transfer Talk』が最新情報をお伝えする。

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Mesloub to replace Gabriel at Man United?
articles.description: Could Lens winger Mezian Mesloub be Manchester United's latest teenage signing? Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：メスルーブがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドでガブリエルの後任に？
articles.descriptionJa: ランスのウインガー、メジアン・メスルーブがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの新たな10代の補強となるか？ トランスファー・トークが最新情報をお届けします。

articles.headline: Hawks rookie Henri Veesaar (ACL) expected to miss season
articles.description: Hawks rookie 7-footer Henri Veesaar suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during a workout last week and is expected to miss the season.
articles.headlineJa: ホークスのルーキー、アンリ・ヴェサール（前十字靭帯）が今季全休の見込み
articles.descriptionJa: ホークスのルーキーで身長7フィートのアンリ・ヴェサールは、先週のワークアウト中に右膝前十字靭帯（ACL）を断裂し、今シーズンを全休する見込みです。

articles.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
articles.description: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including Pelle Larsson getting a long-term extension with the Heat.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NBAの噂：最新のフリーエージェント＆トレード情報
articles.descriptionJa: ペッレ・ラーションがヒートと長期延長契約を結んだ件を含め、NBA全体の契約、トレード、噂を追跡しています。

articles.headline: Nicolas Batum announces retirement after 18 NBA seasons
articles.description: Nicolas Batum has announced his retirement after 18 NBA seasons. A mainstay of the French national team, Batum played most of his NBA career with the Clippers, Hornets and Blazers.
articles.headlineJa: ニコラ・バトゥムがNBA18シーズンのキャリアを経て現役引退を発表
articles.descriptionJa: ニコラ・バトゥムがNBAで18シーズンプレーした後に現役引退を発表しました。フランス代表の主力であったバトゥムは、NBAキャリアの大部分をクリッパーズ、ホーネッツ、ブレイザーズで過ごしました。

articles.headline: Doc Rivers joins NBC as analyst, says coaching career over
articles.description: Doc Rivers turned down an offer to become an NBA analyst for NBC after retiring as a player in 1996 because he couldn't promise then-NBC Sports chairman Dick Ebersol that he wouldn't become a coach.
articles.headlineJa: ドック・リバースがアナリストとしてNBCに加入、監督キャリアの終了を表明
articles.descriptionJa: ドック・リバースは1996年に選手引退後、当時のNBCスポーツ会長ディック・エバーソルに「コーチにならない」と約束できなかったため、NBCのNBAアナリスト就任要請を断っていました。

articles.headline: Clippers name lawyer John Gibson interim governor
articles.description: Los Angeles-based trial lawyer John Gibson will serve as the Clippers' interim governor. He will take over for Steve Ballmer, who has been suspended one year following an investigation into salary cap circumvention.
articles.headlineJa: クリッパーズ、弁護士のジョン・ギブソンを暫定オーナー（ガバナー）に指名
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルスを拠点とする法廷弁護士のジョン・ギブソンが、クリッパーズの暫定ガバナーに就任します。サラリーキャップ回避の調査を受けて1年間の停職処分となったスティーブ・バルマーの後任を務めます。
